narratives.Overview:
## Summary

The Cursor **`/preflight-loop`** command (parallel adversarial review before `git push`) requires launching five `Task` subagents per iteration: Correctness, Security, Performance, Simplification, and optionally Compliance. On a Directive consumer with fail-closed `preToolUse` hooks, **all five spawns fail** with the implement-class worktree-destination deny. The parent agent falls back to manual in-session review, which defeats the purpose of the gate.

This is a **consumer harness / agent-experience** failure at the intersection of:
1. First-party Cursor review subagent types (`bugbot`, `security-review`, unmarked review lanes)
2. Directive `#4066` implement-class spawn dest requirement
3. Cursor `Task` schema stripping `isolation` / `worktree_path` / `cwd` (forum [#171088](https://forum.cursor.com/t/task-spawn-schema-strips-worktree-destination-fail-closed-pretooluse-hooks-cannot-isolate-subagents/171088/12))

## Field instance

| | |
|---|---|
| **When** | 2026-09-10 |
| **Consumer** | [deftai/BestiMax](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax) |
| **Story** | [#306](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/issues/306) — logo upload progress + processing summary |
| **Host** | Cursor, Multitask Mode, `Task` tool |
| **Branch / code** | `feat/306-logo-upload-progress-summary` in linked worktree `.deft-scratch/worktrees/306-logo-upload-progress` |
| **Workspace root** | Primary checkout `/Users/baba/development/BestiMax` (Cursor payload root) |
| **Directive deposit** | `@deftai/directive-core` global hook via `.cursor/hooks.json` `preToolUse` matcher `Task\|SubagentStart\|spawn_subagent\|…` |

**Intent:** read-only pre-push adversarial review (`/preflight-loop` iteration 1). No product writes from subagents. Review target: `origin/develop..HEAD` diff in the worktree.

**Spawn attempted (×5 in parallel):** `Task` with `subagent_type` `bugbot`, `security-review`, and `generalPurpose` review lanes (Correctness / Performance / Simplification / Compliance prompts).

**Deny (class):**

```text
Directive denied implement-class spawn: no worktree destination on the spawn payload
(tool_input.isolation=worktree, worktree_path, or cwd).
```

Subagents never started. Parent completed preflight manually; push proceeded only after a second manual review round.

## Why this is distinct from nearby issues

| Issue | Overlap | Gap this issue covers |
|---|---|---|
| [#4294](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4294) | Cloud `environment` carve-out for implement Task | Does not cover **local** preflight review lanes or read-only review subagent types |
| [#4295](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4295) | Swarm envelope when Task cannot prove local dest | Swarm/product implement framing; not the **preflight-loop** push gate |
| [#4279](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4279) | Deny copy lists unsatisfiable Cursor dest keys | Copy fix only; does not establish a **review-lane spawn posture** |
| [#3866](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3866) | Spawn readiness judged at `payloadRoot` | Ritual/origin-freshness cross-root coupling; preflight hit **dest-missing** first |
| [#1185](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/1185) | `explore` subagent read-only path | Preflight-loop spec names **Bugbot / Security / lane-specific** reviewers, not `explore` |

Core gap: **preflight-loop is a first-party Cursor workflow that depends on parallel review Task spawns, but Directive classifies those spawns as implement-class mutations requiring a local worktree destination the codec cannot send.**

## Expected behaviour

One of (document + implement — pick the honest envelope):

1. **Review-lane posture** — Known read-only review `subagent_type` values used by `/preflight-loop` (`bugbot`, `security-review`, and/or a dedicated review lane type) bypass implement-class dest consult (same honesty class as `explore` / process-only critic), while staying fail-closed for product implement spawns.
2. **Worktree-aware parent spawn** — When the parent session holds a valid occupancy lease on a linked worktree and the Task prompt names `Full Repository Path: <worktree>`, allow read-only review spawns without requiring stripped dest keys on `tool_input`.
3. **Cloud review envelope** — Document that preflight-loop review lanes MUST use `environment: "cloud"` once [#4294](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4294) ships; until then, fail with **satisfiable** recovery text (not unsatisfiable `worktree_path`).
4. **Operator escape hatch** — Explicit `DEFT_SESSION_POSTURE=assist` or preflight-specific marker that allows review Task spawns from the parent checkout without weakening implement gates for feature work.

Whichever envelope ships, **`/preflight-loop` must be able to run its parallel lanes without manual parent substitution** on a standard Directive consumer.

## Repro sketch

1. Consumer repo with Directive hooks on Cursor (`Task` matched in `preToolUse`, `failClosed: true`).
2. Active linked worktree with in-flight feature branch and committed diff vs `develop`.
3. Parent Cursor session rooted at primary checkout; occupancy/ritual satisfied on the worktree.
4. Invoke `/preflight-loop` (or manually launch five review `Task` calls as the command specifies).
5. Observe implement-class dest-missing deny on every spawn.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `/preflight-loop` parallel review `Task` spawns succeed on Cursor + Directive consumer **or** the command docs + deny text name a single satisfiable recovery path (not manual parent review as the only option).
- [ ] Read-only review subagent types used by preflight-loop are not gated as implement-class local mutations requiring `worktree_path` / `isolation` / `cwd` on Cursor.
- [ ] Implement-class product spawns remain fail-closed without dest (#4066 preserved).
- [ ] Deny text on remaining blocks lists satisfiable Cursor recoveries only ([#4279](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/4279) alignment).
- [ ] Tests: hook fixture for preflight-style review Task allow + implement Task deny without dest.
- [ ] CHANGELOG + consumer note (BestiMax `/preflight-loop` rule references this).

## Related

- BestiMax [#306](https://github.com/deftai/BestiMax/issues/306) / branch `feat/306-logo-upload-progress-summary` (field instance)
- Cursor forum: [Task spawn schema strips worktree destination](https://forum.cursor.com/t/task-spawn-schema-strips-worktree-destination-fail-closed-pretooluse-hooks-cannot-isolate-subagents/171088/12)

## Verdict on the recorded target

The target is a conjunction and the halves do not share a fate.

- **"Directive classifies /preflight-loop review Task spawns (bugbot, security-review, generalPurpose review lanes) as implement-class"** — **survives, measured.** Only three spawn classes reach an allow ahead of the dest consult: `explore` (`dispatcher.ts:2587`), the Grok-only process-only class (`:2603`), and ephemeral/assist (`:2646`). `bugbot` / `security-review` / `generalPurpose` match none, so they fall to `inspectMutationGates` at `dispatcher.ts:2660`.
- **"requiring a local worktree destination the Cursor codec cannot send"** — **does not survive as a claim about Directive.** Directive accepts a Cursor `Task` destination today and allows the spawn: `dispatcher-spawn-dest.test.ts:563` "keeps Cursor Task dest occupancy and envelope rewrite" drives `host: "cursor"`, `tool_name: "Task"`, `tool_input: { subagent_type: "generalPurpose", isolation: "worktree" }` and asserts `verdict: "allow"`, `code: "spawn-ready"` plus an `updatedInput` rewrite of `tool_input.isolation` and a minted `incarnation`. The unsendability is a claim about the Cursor client, and this repository has explicitly recorded it as **unbound** (finding 1).
- The implied third clause — that the lanes therefore cannot run without manual parent substitution — **falls.** At the dispatch SHA there is exactly one per-spawn satisfiable Cursor `Task` allow for a read-only lane, `subagent_type: explore`, and the body dismisses it by name rather than by capability.

**Evidence.** `packages/core/src/session/spawn-occupancy.ts:105-107`:

```text
const HOSTS_THAT_REROOT = new Set(["claude", "cursor", "codex"]);
// #4279: Cursor Task dest-key bind waits on a recorded PreToolUse payload.
// HOSTS_THAT_REROOT for Task stays unbound until that measurement.
```

`xbrief/completed/2026-09-10-4279-bughookscursor-implement-class-task-deny-names-dest-fields-c.xbrief.json`, item 0 `Do not bind deny-copy until Task payload is measured`, `x-directive.disposition.disposition: "deferred"`, reason: *"No recorded Cursor Task PreToolUse dest payload. Isolation-key bind and HOSTS_THAT_REROOT / host-cursor.md Step 2e for Task stay unbound."* That file is the only content of commit 781be07a — the dispatch SHA of this arc.

`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher-spawn-dest.test.ts:563` (above) is the behavioural half: the predicate does not merely tolerate a Cursor `Task` dest key, it allows on one, and `HOSTS_THAT_REROOT` membership means `isolation: "worktree"` with no path also allows (`spawn-occupancy.ts:428` guard is skipped because `hostCanReroot` is true at `:366`).

If a Cursor `Task` carrying `isolation: "worktree"` does reach `tool_input` — which Directive's own predicate, its `HOSTS_THAT_REROOT` membership, its `updatedInput` rewrite, and `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-cursor.md:17` ("The worktree path set to the agent's isolated git worktree") all presuppose — then the gate is already per-spawn satisfiable and every carve-out is a gratuitous authority widening. If it does not, then `HOSTS_THAT_REROOT` membership for `Task`, host-cursor.md:17, the eight-key deny copy, and the test at :563 are all wrong together, and that is a much larger build than a review-lane posture.

The "Why this is distinct" table makes this worse rather than better: it reduces #4279 to "Copy fix only; does not establish a review-lane spawn posture" and drops the one blocking finding #4279's arc accepted into contract, which is precisely this measurement. #4295 does carry the premise with a named source (Cursor staff on forum #171088, "No per-spawn `isolation` / `worktree_path` / `cwd` on `Task`") — but that is an attributed third-party claim, and #4279 item 0 was deferred *after* it, on the ground that no PreToolUse payload has been recorded. So the two candidate owners of this fact both point at the same open measurement.

**Disposition consequence.** No option premised on unsendability can bind before that one observation. The honest scope for this arc is either the measurement itself, or a recorded dependency edge onto #4295/#4279 item 0 — not four solution envelopes stacked on the unbound fact. Nothing here rests on "a reviewer would catch it": the deterministic control is item 0's own acceptance clause, already written and already deferred.

## 2. blocks-the-design — option 1 is an implement bypass by type-name, and it collides with a rule pinned into every consumer AGENTS.md

*(a) #2308 review-surface precedence, in the always-pinned set.* `content/templates/agents-entry.md:118`, `AGENTS.md:54`, `AGENTS.md:280`, `content/packs/rules/rules-pack-0.1.json:3658` all carry the same MUST: route review work through `deft-directive-review-cycle`; host `babysit` / `bugbot` / `security-review` **advisory-only**. `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md:265-269` names those exact Cursor subagent types and says a generic review request "must NOT be routed to those host-native tools as the review of record", with host tools folded in "as *advisory* finding sources ... never as a replacement". `/preflight-loop` uses `bugbot` and `security-review` as the review of record before push.

**Failure mode.** `subagent_type` on a `Task` payload is caller-typed text. An allowlist on the strings `bugbot` / `security-review` is a one-token implement bypass any spawn can type, and unlike `plan` / `process_only` those are not markers implement-class never sets — they are first-party names an implementing spawn has every reason to type, and a custom agent name can be typed too. The `hasImplementConflictSignal` fence narrows but does not close it: a review lane carries no `drive_to`, `worker_role`, or `dispatch_kind` to conflict on, so the fence is vacuous for exactly this class. The deterministic control the design needs is the shape #4296 already names: a marker the implement path never emits, composed with the conflict fence. A type-name allowlist is not that shape. Note also that the read-only capability signal cannot serve as the allow token unaided — `dispatcher.ts:2583` *denies* a read-only non-explore spawn (`read-only posture blocks implementation sub-agent spawns`), so read-only posture makes this deny stricter, not looser.

## 3. blocks-the-design — option 2 asks the seam to classify from prompt text and to inherit the parent dest, which are two standing refusals

**Evidence.** `spawn-occupancy.ts:157-160`: *"Spawn destination from tool_input only. Top-level payload cwd is the parent's hook execution directory -- treating it as the child destination would inherit cwd, which this seam refuses."* `readonly.ts:238`: *"Free-text prompt strings are never classified."* `readonly.ts:359`: *"Prompt text is never a class."* Option 2's stated trigger is "the Task prompt names `Full Repository Path: <worktree>`".

**Failure mode.** The prompt is the untrusted channel on this exact surface — a preflight review prompt embeds a diff and issue/PR text by construction. A destination read out of prompt text lets ingested content name the destination. Beyond injection, it breaks the uniqueness half of #4066: `mintImplementSpawnReservation` / `evaluateImplementSpawnOccupancy` (`spawn-occupancy.ts:554`, `:595`) reserve a destination uniquely per spawn, and five parallel lanes naming one prompt-stated worktree path are a reservation conflict by design. "Parent holds a lease on a linked worktree" plus a prompt-named path is inherit-cwd with extra steps.

**Disposition consequence.** Strike option 2 from the option set rather than carrying it as a peer envelope. #4295 already closes this space at three envelopes and explicitly forbids inventing a fourth.

## 4. sharpens-framing — the option set is not four peers: one is shipped, one is owned elsewhere, one is refused

**Evidence.** Option 4's mechanism ships today. `readonly.ts:12-25` `ASSIST_POSTURE_MARKERS` includes `assist`; `hasSessionAssistEphemeralEnv` (`:225`) reads `DEFT_SESSION_POSTURE`; `isEphemeralSpawn` (`:241`) returns true on it; and `dispatcher.ts:2646-2659` returns `spawn-ephemeral-ready` **before** `inspectMutationGates` at `:2660`, so the dest consult never runs (#3259 D1-B / #1802). Option 3 is #4294 (open) plus #4295 envelope 2 (`design-critique:ingest-ready`, in implementation), and #4295's own framing is "This issue tracks the **host adapter + swarm envelope**, not the hook dest carve-out."

**Failure mode.** `DEFT_SESSION_POSTURE` is session-scoped, so setting it to allow the five review lanes also ephemeral-allows the *feature* implement spawns in the same Cursor session — exactly what option 4's own text says it must not do ("without weakening implement gates for feature work"). Presented as a fourth thing to build, the option hides that its mechanism already exists and already fails the constraint attached to it. A builder reading four peers ships the env var, satisfies the acceptance box, and silently opens the session's implement gate.

**Disposition consequence.** Re-cut the option set before binding: shipped-and-inadequate (4, with the session-scope reason recorded), owned-elsewhere (3 → #4294 / #4295), refused (2, finding 3), needs-a-new-class-shape (1, finding 2). Only after that re-cut is there a scope this arc can hold.

## 5. sharpens-framing — the deny quoted as evidence no longer exists, and the copy that replaced it names a Grok-only recovery on Cursor
